name: Altstadt
tagline: Inside the Promenade ring, with the cathedral market
description: The historic core enclosed by the tree-lined Promenade that replaced the city walls, holding the cathedral, the Prinzipalmarkt arcades and the town hall where the Peace of Westphalia was signed. The Saturday market on the cathedral square is one of the best in Germany. Everything is walkable or a two-minute cycle.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the market, the arcades and the Promenade at the door
pros: The cathedral market and the whole centre on foot
Promenade cycle ring immediately around it
Best restaurant and cafe density in the city
cons: The highest rents in an already tight market
Busy with shoppers and visitors through the day

name: Kuhviertel
tagline: The old student quarter, with Pinkus Muller still brewing
description: The historic student district on the northwestern edge of the Altstadt, where the Pinkus Muller brewery has operated since 1816 and the old pubs around it still fill with students. Narrow streets, small flats and a genuine neighbourhood feel two minutes from the cathedral.
bestFor: Stays that want the old pubs and the centre without living on the market square
pros: Traditional pubs and the brewery on the street
Two minutes from the cathedral and the Promenade
More neighbourhood character than the Altstadt proper
cons: Noise from the pubs on term-time nights
Small, old flats with variable fittings

name: Hafen
tagline: The converted inland harbour, bars and creative offices
description: The Dortmund-Ems canal basin southeast of the station, where the old warehouses have been turned into bars, clubs, restaurants and studios along the water. It is the centre of the city's nightlife and its newest apartments, and the cycle route into the Altstadt takes about seven minutes.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the bars and clubs on the doorstep and a modern flat
pros: The main concentration of nightlife in the city
Station and Altstadt both a short cycle away
cons: Rents rising steadily with the redevelopment

name: Aaseestadt and Geist
tagline: Around the lake, family-quiet and green
description: The residential districts south and west of the Aasee, the lake that functions as the city's main recreation ground with rowing, running paths and the open-air museum on its far shore. Housing is mostly post-war blocks and family houses, quieter than the centre and a ten-minute cycle from it.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a run round the lake and a quieter street
pros: The Aasee and its paths immediately there
Rents below the Altstadt and Hafen
Ten-minute cycle to the centre on dedicated paths
cons: Little going on in the evening
Fewer shops than the central districts

name: Gievenbeck and the University Districts
tagline: West of the centre, where the students and the cheap rents are
description: The western districts around the university's science campuses and the halls of residence, built as estates and student housing with supermarkets, sports facilities and a large student population. Rents are the lowest in the city and the cycle into the Altstadt takes about fifteen minutes.
bestFor: Budget stays connected to the university, with a bike as standard equipment
pros: University facilities and cheap eating nearby
Flat, safe cycle route into the centre
cons: Fifteen minutes by bike to the Altstadt
